subject: Clarify output rights & training carve-outs — MSA + Order Form
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily@vertex.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Vertex Solutions Procurement <procurement@vertex.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on output ownership + training (Order Form v3 redlines)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week — we had a productive discussion with our infra team. As we run the redline pass on the Order Form + MSA, there are a few items in sections related to output ownership and training that our legal and procurement teams want clarified before we proceed to signatures.

High-level asks:
- Confirm whether Vertex retains exclusive rights to outputs (model responses) generated from our prompts and data.
- Clarify Redwood's feedback license: do you require the right to use customer content or outputs to improve models? If so, can that be limited to de-identified logs only and excluded for certain regulated workloads?
- We are requesting an explicit carve-out: no training on Vertex data without separate written consent (we can consider a scoped, opt-in program).

I attached our redlines to the Order Form (Vertex_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf). Can you confirm Redwood's standard position and propose language we can exchange? Procurement would like a tentative path to signature this week if possible.

Thanks,
Emily Zhao
Senior Procurement Manager
Vertex Solutions
[Attachment: Vertex_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf (PDF, 42 KB)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily@vertex.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on output ownership + training (Order Form v3 redlines)

Emily — thanks for the clear note and for sending the redlines. I've looped in our legal lead (Laura Bennett) and contracts (Karthik) to propose concrete language.

Quick summary of Redwood's typical stance:
- Output ownership: Customers keep rights to outputs. We don't claim ownership of customer prompts or generated outputs in our standard MSA; we typically grant customers a perpetual license to use outputs.
- Feedback/license: We request a limited, non-exclusive feedback license to use de-identified logs to improve models and our service. Customers can opt out for regulated workloads via an order form checkbox or an addendum.
- Training on customer data: Redwood does not train models on raw customer data without explicit opt-in; we can offer a customer-approved, scoped training program for an additional commercial commitment.

That said, your redlines introduce some stricter language around exclusivity and training carve-outs that we'll need to reconcile. Laura / Karthik — can you review the attached PDF and propose language we can send back to Vertex by EOD? I'd like to keep the signature timeline but not at the expense of leaving regulatory customers unprotected.

Soojin
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: Vertex_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf]

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on output ownership + training (internal)

Soojin / Karthik — initial thoughts after skimming Vertex redlines (see attached MSA redline doc):

1) Output ownership: Vertex's redline attempts to make outputs "exclusive property" of Vertex and to prohibit Redwood from retaining any derivative rights. That's broader than our standard model — customers have rights to outputs, but Redwood must retain the ability to use aggregated/derived learnings for product improvement (we do not use verbatim outputs as training material unless customer opts in). Proposed compromise: Add express language that customers own outputs but Redwood retains a limited right to use aggregated, de-identified metrics/derivatives that cannot be traced to Vertex. Sample clause: "Customer retains ownership of Outputs. Provider may use aggregated and de-identified Outputs and telemetry for the sole purpose of improving Provider's services, provided such use does not include Customer Identifiers or verbatim Customer Content."

2) Feedback/training: Vertex wants a broad prohibition on training on any Outputs or Input without prior written consent — they requested the opt-in be the default. We should accept opt-in for model training (commercial addendum) and provide an explicit opt-out checkbox for the hosted product for regulated customers. Also include a narrow exception for security/bug-fix telemetry (non-training use).

3) Order form checkbox: Recommend we offer a checkbox in the Order Form for "Opt into Redwood model training using de-identified logs" and a separate line-item price if they want dedicated model customization. This preserves business upside.

4) Definitions: We must define "Outputs", "Customer Content", "De-identified", and "Training" clearly in the MSA. Vertex redlines currently lack a clear definition of "de-identified" — propose referencing a standard (e.g., removal of PII per our internal spec) and allowing Customer to audit on notice.

I'll draft language for 1–2 and mark the redline. Karthik, if you can check the commercial fallback (checkbox + addendum) and pricing callouts, we can push a clean markup external by EOD.

Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redline_MSA_Section7_training.docx]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily@vertex.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on output ownership + training (Order Form v3 redlines) — proposed language

Emily — attached is a clean markup with our suggested language and a short summary of tradeoffs (see Redline_MSA_Section7_training.docx). Key points we propose to send to Vertex legal: 

- Ownership: "Customer retains ownership of Outputs."
- Provider use: "Provider may use aggregated, de-identified Outputs and telemetry solely to improve Provider services; such use will exclude Customer Identifiers and verbatim Customer Content."
- Training opt-in: "Provider will not use Customer Content or Outputs to train Provider models without Customer's separate written consent. Customer may opt into a scoped training/customization program via Order Form or Addendum."
- Opt-out for regulated workloads: "For the avoidance of doubt, Customer may designate data as Regulated Data; Provider shall not use Regulated Data for training or model improvements unless Customer provides prior written consent."

Attached: Redline_MSA_Section7_training.docx (contains exact redline edits) and a one-pager for procurement that shows two commercial paths (hosted opt-out vs paid customization).

Next steps: If those points look acceptable, can you confirm which sections Vertex would like stricter wording on (exclusivity, audit rights, definition of de-identified)? We can produce a final redline for execution. HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/RDW-2027-459

Best,
Soojin
[Attachments: Redline_MSA_Section7_training.docx (DOCX, 18 KB); Redwood_Training_Options_1pager.pdf (PDF, 6 KB)]
